text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT 2026-03-22 resolved — summary: synchronized TTL expiries + a config deploy that disabled prefix cache in ap-south caused a surge of origin fetches. Immediate mitigation: rolled back deploy and ran targeted priming. Full PM: https://redwood.link/pm-1771304022

Maya SRE: copying postmortem notes here. Main outcomes: 1) immediate runbook updates for cache storms, 2) tighter early-warning alerts, 3) review SLO windowing for tail latency.

Raj (eng-runtime): root cause: a deploy removed a caching optimization flag in one service matrix, TTLs were aligned because a previous job reset them. I've got a branch that adds jittered TTLs and a backpressure cap on origin fetch concurrency. Will open PR.

Priya (product): customers in APAC saw spikes on long tail; do we want to change public SLA language or keep that stable and adjust internal SLOs?

Clara (eng-sre lead): maintain public SLA for now. Adjust internal SLOs and introduce automatic product alerts when error budget consumption crosses a threshold. If we observe repeat incidents (>=2) within 30 days, re-evaluate public SLA.

Ben (observability): proposed alert + dashboard work:
- Early-warning: 3m derivative on cache_miss_ratio > 0.12 -> route to #eng-oncall (owner: Ben) -> due 2026-03-26
- Region TTL heatmap panel + 30d rolling p99 widget (owner: Ben) -> due 2026-03-29
- Error budget burn alert: notify product at 25% remaining, page infra at 10% remaining (owner: Clara) -> due 2026-03-27

Raj (eng-runtime): tactical controls I'll add: per-region fetch concurrency cap + conservative re-enable of prefix caching. Also will add a canary job that applies cache-related config to one zone and validates miss-rate for 30m before global rollout. Owner: Raj -> due 2026-03-31.

Maya SRE: runbook updates (short checklist) I will add:
1) identify hot routes (top 10 by miss volume)
2) run priming job (example below)
3) rollback config -> contact runtime lead
Runbook snippet:
```bash
# find hot routes
redwoodctl metrics query "sum by(route) (increase(cache_miss_total[15m])) | sort_desc(10)"
# prime routes (parallel small batches)
redwoodctl cache prime --routes-file /tmp/hot_routes.txt --region ap-south --batch-size 4 --delay 5s
# rollback last deploy for service
redwoodctl deploy rollback --service inference-runtime --to 2026-03-22T09:12:00Z
```

Priya (product): SLO proposal draft: keep median and p95 as-is, change p99 to rolling 30d with product notification on budget <25%. Also add a customer notification playbook (template + owners) in case SLA remediation is required later. Owner: Priya -> due 2026-03-28.

Clara (eng-sre lead): SLO thresholds for now:
- p50: 40ms (unchanged)
- p95: 120ms (unchanged)
- p99: 300ms, window: rolling 30d, alert when 7d burn rate > 1.5x baseline OR remaining budget < 25%
Add dashboards: 30d rolling p99, 7d burn, per-region p99, and capacity fallback status. Owner: Ben -> due 2026-03-29.

Ben (observability): will run a retro query for similar "cache alignment" incidents over past 180 days and post counts + examples. If occurrences >= 2 per 90d we escalate to priority remediation. Due: 2026-03-25.

Maya SRE: quick prometheus alert prototype I'll add to the repo (tweak thresholds as we iterate):
```yaml
- alert: CacheMissDerivative
  expr: (increase(cache_miss_total[3m]) / increase(requests_total[3m])) - (increase(cache_miss_total[12m]) / increase(requests_total[12m])) > 0.08
  for: 1m
  labels:
    severity: high
  annotations:
    summary: "Rapid increase in cache miss ratio in {{ $labels.region }}"
```

Raj (eng-runtime): opened draft PR for jittered TTL + fetch cap: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/462. Tests added include canary job and e2e for cache priming.

Clara (eng-sre lead): action item summary (owners + due dates):
- Runbook update (Maya) -> 2026-03-24
- Early-warning alert + routing (Ben) -> 2026-03-26
- Dashboard panels + 30d p99 (Ben) -> 2026-03-29
- Canary config rollout + fetch cap (Raj) -> 2026-03-31
- Product customer note template + notification playbook (Priya) -> 2026-03-28
- SLO RFC for p99 rolling window (Clara) -> 2026-03-27
- Retro lookback for recurring incidents (Ben) -> 2026-03-25

Maya SRE: agree with owners. I'll link every PR and dashboard in the PM and we'll use weekly follow-ups until items closed.

Priya (product): tagging legal/comms once we have the customer template ready.

oncall-bot: Reminder: weekly follow-up scheduled Fridays 09:00 UTC until thread resolved.

Clara (eng-sre lead): thanks team. No public SLA change today. We will reconvene after the SLO RFC and retro results to decide if any public-facing commitments need updating. :thumbsup:
